title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Nauru: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Nauru: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: When a death occurs in Nauru, immediate mortuary limits make prompt medical coordination and civil notification essential. Because Nauru's statutory portal (ronlaw.gov.nr) relies on an interactive viewer and domestic ministry websites publish directories rather than detailed step-by-step procedural pages online, this checklist draws directly on primary Nauru legislation, Government Gazette and directory filings, Naoero Super publications, and accredited regional diplomatic guidance [1][2][4][7][10].

steps.title: Immediate medical certification, mortuary limits, and coronial rules
steps.html:
• Contact emergency services on 118 (ambulance/medical) or 117 (police/fire) if death occurs outside medical care [11]. For hospital deaths, obtain the medical certificate of cause of death from the attending medical officer at Republic of Nauru Hospital [10].
  • Coordinate funeral arrangements without delay: diplomatic consular reporting documents that Nauru has no formal funeral homes, no embalming or cremation facilities, no metal/lead-lined caskets, and no long-term hospital mortuary capacity, meaning non-suspicious deaths are generally released within roughly 24 hours for local burial using locally made plywood caskets (typically around US$ 300) [10].
  • Where a death is sudden, unexplained, or occurs in custody, Nauru Police investigate and a Resident Magistrate may conduct a statutory inquiry under Section 7 of the Inquests Act 1977 (with Section 8 governing any exhumation); note that Nauru lacks resident forensic pathology services for internal autopsies [10].

steps.title: Civil death registration within the 14-day statutory deadline
steps.html:
• Notify and register the death with the Registrar of Births, Deaths and Marriages inside the Department of Justice and Border Control within 14 days of the date of death (or discovery), as mandated under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 2017 (which entered into force on 1 February 2018) [1][3].
  • Submit the hospital death notification, identification details of the deceased person, and informant particulars through Department of Justice and Border Control [1][3][4].
  • Request multiple certified Death Certificate extracts immediately for Naoero Super, Curator estate settlement, bank closures, and overseas diplomatic procedures [2][7][10].

steps.title: Naoero Super (SuperLife) and public-service death benefits
steps.html:
• Notify Naoero Super (SuperLife) promptly if the person contributed to Nauru's national superannuation fund, using the Naoero Super Death and TPD Withdrawal Form [7][8][9]. Claims require the certified Death Certificate, proof of beneficiary identity, and where applicable court probate or letters of administration [7][8].
  • If the person was employed in the Republic's public service, notify human resources promptly regarding final salary and leave balances under the Public Service Act 2016 and the Public Service (Amendment) Act 2018 [5][6]. Under Section 103(3) added by the 2018 Amendment Act, where a public officer dies (or is presumed dead) before reaching 12 years' service, the Chief Secretary may authorise a gratuity payment to dependants [6].

steps.title: Office of the Curator of Intestate Estates and Nauru Revenue Office
steps.html:
• Contact Office of the Curator of Intestate Estates within Justice and Border Control (justice.gov.nr) regarding estate administration under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act 1976 [2]. The Curator administers intestate estates, and may also step in on testate estates if no executor resides in Nauru or no grant application is made within 3 months of death [2].
  • Expect a formal Gazette notice and a statutory 21-day waiting period before the Curator makes asset payouts (subject to any Nauru Lands Committee claims or court injunctions), and furnish Bendigo Bank agency account particulars for authorised disbursements [2].
  • Contact Nauru Revenue Office (First Floor, Civic Centre, Aiwo; +674 557 3238; cashier Monday to Thursday 9:30 AM to 4:00 PM, Friday 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM) to settle any final employment tax or business tax returns; Nauru does not levy a separate inheritance or estate tax [4].

steps.title: Consular legalisation and notifying banks and institutions
steps.html:
• Confirm overseas authentication requirements before mailing official records: Nauru is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Nauru Death Certificates and court or Curator documents for foreign use require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than an Apostille [12].
  • Notify employers, Bendigo Bank agency/Nauru banking services, utility accounts, and the Nauru Media Corporation or land offices in writing with certified Death Certificate extracts [2][4][13].
  • Keep a complete binder of hospital certificates, Registry receipts, Naoero Super confirmations, and Curator correspondence for family or international settlement [2][8][10].

contacts.name: Office of the Curator of Intestate Estates
contacts.note: Administers intestate and qualifying testate estates under the Succession, Probate and Administration Act 1976 (3-month threshold and 21-day Gazette period).

contacts.name: Naoero Super (SuperLife)
contacts.note: Administers Nauru's national superannuation fund, processing member Death and TPD claims via SuperLife.

contacts.note: First Floor, Civic Centre, Aiwo; handles final employment and business tax clearances (cashier Mon-Thu 9:30 AM-4:00 PM, Fri 9:30 AM-4:30 PM).
